blocks.text: THE VISION OF OBADIAH (OBADIAH 1) · TWO KINGDOMS
Obadiah. Twenty-one verses against Edom, for standing by when strangers entered Jerusalem's gates.
SCRIPTURE CALLS
Prophet
ERA
Two kingdoms 930–586 BC
IN THE DAYS OF
No ruler named beside him
BOOK
Obadiah
HOW THE WORD CAME
The book is called “The vision of Obadiah”, and the words are the LORD's: “Thus saith the Lord GOD concerning Edom; We have heard a rumour from the LORD”.
THE CALL
How the word came
The book is called “The vision of Obadiah”, and the words are the LORD's: “Thus saith the Lord GOD concerning Edom; We have heard a rumour from the LORD”. Obadiah 1:1
THE MESSAGE
The word in its main themes
Edom's pride brought down
“The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee, thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock”
Obadiah 1:3 (KJV) →
“Though thou exalt thyself as the eagle, and though thou set thy nest among the stars, thence will I bring thee down, saith the LORD.”
Obadiah 1:4 (KJV) →
Violence against thy brother Jacob
“For thy violence against thy brother Jacob shame shall cover thee, and thou shalt be cut off for ever.”
Obadiah 1:10 (KJV) →
As thou hast done
“as thou hast done, it shall be done unto thee: thy reward shall return upon thine own head.”
Obadiah 1:15 (KJV) →
Mount Zion, and the kingdom the LORD's
“And saviours shall come up on mount Zion to judge the mount of Esau; and the kingdom shall be the LORD’s.”
Obadiah 1:21 (KJV) →
THE WORD TO …
To whom the word was spoken
TO EDOM
“Thou shouldest not have entered into the gate of my people in the day of their calamity”
Obadiah 1:13 (KJV) →
THE BOOK
The book of Obadiah
1 Edom brought down Obadiah 1:1–9
2 The day of thy brother Obadiah 1:10–14
3 The day of the LORD; Zion and the kingdom Obadiah 1:15–21
HOW THE STORY ENDS
Scripture says, tradition says
SCRIPTURE SAYS
From the textScripture says nothing of this Obadiah beyond the title of his book. Obadiah 1:1
TRADITION SAYS
No tradition is recorded here.
OPEN QUESTIONS
Where readers have differed
Under Jehoram of Judah
C. F. Keil (1868)

Philistines and Arabians broke into Judah in Jehoram's day (2 Chr 21:16–17). Keil: “there only remains the taking of Jerusalem by the Philistines and Arabians in the time of Jehoram”. 2 Chronicles 21:16–17 [9]
In Amaziah's reign
Seder Olam, as reported by the Jewish Encyclopedia (1905)
“The prophecy of Obadiah occurred in the time of Amaziah, King of Judah”.[42]
Early, foretelling the Babylonian capture
E. B. Pusey (The Minor Prophets, 1860–77)
Pusey reads verses 11–14 as a prediction of Nebuchadnezzar's siege, and holds that since Obadiah came before Jeremiah “it was probably long anterior to it.”[47][45]
After the fall of Jerusalem in 586
S. R. Driver (1891); G. A. Smith (1898), for verses 10–21

Driver: the expressions in verses 11–14 “are most naturally referred to the destruction of Jerusalem by the Chaldaeans in 586”. Smith takes verses 10–21 so, but holds that verses 1–9 “probably reflect earlier events”. Obadiah 1:11–14 Psalms 137:7 [3][45]
IN SCRIPTURE
Every passage
CHAPTERS · 2
Obadiah 1 Jeremiah 49
PASSAGES · 2
Obadiah 1:1–21 Jeremiah 49:7–22
WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture gives no father, home, king or date for Obadiah.
The text does not say whether he is any of the other men named Obadiah, such as Ahab's steward (1 Kgs 18:3).
The book does not name the strangers who entered Jerusalem's gates (Obad 11); which attack is meant is the question of its date.
The New Testament does not quote Obadiah.
